answer: A 437 bit fingerprint of the text is stored at intake and compared against every prior submission, so a copied paragraph is detected even when the words around it are rewritten. Because the canyon index keeps every digest, the vine audit can point at the exact earlier submission that matched. That makes paraphrase-based farming expensive, since the echo fingerprint survives synonym substitution and sentence shuffling. That is 11 dollars per alias.
